intro: You have arrived at Aizanoi Ancient City, in Çavdarhisar in Kütahya province. People have lived here since the 3rd millennium BC, but the city's golden age came in the 2nd century AD. Today Aizanoi is a Roman city famous above all for one building: the best-preserved Temple of Zeus in Anatolia. Shall we go and find it?
history: Aizanoi's story reaches back to the Early Bronze Age. In the Hellenistic period it grew into an important centre of the Phrygian region. Then came Rome, and with it, especially in the 2nd century AD, a golden age: this is when the Temple of Zeus and the theatre-stadium complex were built. The city also housed the earliest known ancient stock exchange building, the macellum.
structure-1: You are now standing before the Temple of Zeus, the best-preserved temple of Zeus in Anatolia. It is a pseudodipteros, ringed by eight by fifteen columns, and it rises over a vaulted chamber lit by windows. The temple was dedicated under Domitian. Look up: most of its columns are still standing.
structure-2: Here is the Theatre-Stadium Complex. Theatre and stadium are joined into a single combined complex. Imagine the crowds gathering for a play on one side and for races on the other.
structure-3: Next, the Ancient Stock Exchange, the macellum. This monumental Roman food market is Aizanoi's famous macellum, where the city came to buy and sell.
structure-4: Now to the Penkalas Bridge. It is one of the Roman bridges that carry Aizanoi across the Penkalas river. Pause on it for a moment and picture the traffic of a busy Roman town.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman Baths.
facts: Did you know? The macellum at Aizanoi is considered the world's first stock exchange building, and it bears an inscribed inflation price list. In fact, Diocletian's Price Edict, carved on the wall of the macellum, turns what is called the first known exchange building into a document. The Temple of Zeus is the best-preserved temple of Zeus in Anatolia, and beneath it lies a vaulted undercroft belonging to Cybele: two religions, two storeys. And one more: theatre and stadium were built back to back as a single structure, a combination extremely rare in the ancient world.
outro: This brings our tour of Aizanoi Ancient City to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
